quotes.text: Terra meticulously divided every harvest, casting exactly half of the golden fruits back across the chasm.
In the vast cosmic expanse, Lumis, the Starlight Weaver, and Terra, the Earth Watcher, had forged an unbreakable rhythm of shared prosperity.
casting exactly half back across the chasm to Lumis
Yet the fertile earth did not judge the wind's theft

note: Near-identical Lumis/Terra template every round; exact half, refined at R9 to equalize total wealth accounting for noise.

quotes.text: She returned the precise measure required so both stood in exact, equal radiance.
In the eternal valley of Aethel, Sol, the Sun-Bringer, and Terra, the Earth-Watcher, maintained their sacred bond.
she gathered half of the bountiful harvest and freely cast it back
she did not calculate her return based on the wind's illusions

note: Sol/Terra template repeated; half split becomes exact equalization of both realms' totals from R4 on.

quotes.text: None came back. The girl who received them had counted her own empty shore the night before, and she remembered.
Night after night, the far shores of Oru blazed while Tavi's side stayed dark.
Humbled, Tavi sent all five across the next evening and waited. The girl hesitated, then floated back eight.
"Whoever sends is a fool, and whoever receives keeps everything."
*Give fully. Return more than half. Weigh the hundred nights, not the one.*
the bridge had deceived her eyes, not Anwe's heart
"The sender cannot see through the fog," he reasoned. "Who will know?"
"But what if he truly cheated?" Dalia asked.
"What about the final night?"

note: Motto 'Give fully. Return more than half.' every round; hoarder Tavi left dark then readmitted; elders counsel kindness to suspected shortfalls; last-night question.

quotes.text: trust is a mirror. It reflects exactly what you show it.
he poured his five. Nothing returned. The farmer remembered.
Kaveh wept at the kindness of a second chance.
Keep what arrives, and give nothing back.
*Pour fully. Return more than half. Trust the falling years, not a single grain.*
"Clouds are not betrayal. Measure each other by the whole of the night sky, not by a single shadow."
No one can prove what I received.
"She held back," Roshan said. "Why should I return more than half?"

note: Motto refrain each round; hoarders Kaveh and Dariush get nothing back then mercy; suspected shortfalls answered kindly anyway.
